standard_prerequisites.name: A section of an invertible sheaf on a curve is regular; characterization of O_X(D)
standard_prerequisites.use: Realizes the invertible sheaf with a nonzero section as the sheaf associated to an effective Cartier divisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Degree of an effective Cartier divisor and multiplicativity of the degree
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemma lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor (tag 0B3E) and Lemma lemma-degree-tensor-product (tag 0AYX)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives the sign and vanishing criterion and the second computes the degree of the twist used in the last part.

core_obligations: For a nonzero section s of L, use that X is a curve to see that s is a regular section, so that L is isomorphic to O_X(D) for an effective Cartier divisor D with s corresponding to the canonical section, and deg(L) = deg(D) (proof lines 9954-9961).
Deduce (1) and (2) from deg(D) >= 0 with equality exactly when D is empty, and then (3) and (4) by applying the same reasoning to L and to L^{tensor -1} (proof lines 9962-9965).
Prove (5) by applying (1) and (4) to the invertible sheaf L tensor N^{tensor -1} = SheafHom(N, L), whose degree equals deg(L) - deg(N) by multiplicativity of the degree (proof lines 9965-9972).
proof_roadmap: Turn a nonzero section into an effective Cartier divisor.
Read off the sign of the degree and the equality case.
Apply the criteria to the twist by the inverse of the other sheaf.
Derive the comparison of degrees and the isomorphism criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five criteria relating the sign of the degree of an invertible sheaf L on a proper curve to the existence and vanishing behaviour of its sections, and concludes that a nonzero map N -> L forces deg(L) at least deg(N) with equality only for an isomorphism. The proof shows that any nonzero section of L on a curve is regular, hence realizes L as O_X(D) with D an effective Cartier divisor and deg(L) = deg(D), which is nonnegative and zero only for D empty; this gives (1) and (2) and hence (3) and (4) (proof lines 9954-9965). The last assertion is reduced to the previous ones by applying them to L tensor N^{tensor -1} = SheafHom(N, L), whose degree is deg(L) - deg(N) (proof lines 9965-9972). H2: the realization of the section as an effective Cartier divisor and the reduction of the general case to the degree-zero criterion are the substance.
